newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends mixed, pauses after rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends mixed, pauses after rally.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures were narrowly mixed by the finish on Monday after an uninspired session, traders said.
After an encouraging start which saw September hitting a new one-year high as buy-stops were triggered, the market lost momentum and headed lower on light jobber liquidation.
Traders said the market was probably heading for a breather after last week's rally on heavy trade and fund buying.
"The market is resting a bit," said one, saying that the market was trying to build a base after the rally on Thursday and Friday.
"It needs something fresh to get it going again," he added.

September peaked at 1,140 stg per tonne, the highest on the second month since June 16, 1996 and a fresh contract high, before slipping back on trade profit-taking. It ended the day five stg down at 1,123 stg.
Front-month July matched Friday's life-of-contract high at 1,122 stg before finishing nine stg lower at 1,107.
Friday's rally extended Thursday's surge on concerns the developing El Nino weather pattern would spark droughts in major cocoa-producing countries and disrupt next year's cocoa crop.

Though some traders were sceptical of the fundamental change said to be pushing cocoa prices higher, they said they could not ignore the strong uptrend developing on near- and intermediate-term technical charts.
Traders said there was also talk that a U.S. crop forecaster Hans Killian had released what some regarded as a fairly bullish Ivorian crop estimate.
Volume was 6,400 lots. July/Sept switches led actives, finishing the day at 16 stg after trading at 23 last week.
